title: Silent config_db Misses
description: Find four uvm_config_db bugs (a type mismatch, a field name, a scope that does not reach, and a precedence surprise) from the +UVM_CONFIG_DB_TRACE log and the check_config_usage() report.

steps.title: Step 1: Read the first fatal and fix the driver
steps.instructions: Compile src/dv/testbench.sv only, with tb_top as the top module, and run with +UVM_CONFIG_DB_TRACE. The run stops in build_phase with UVM_FATAL [NO_VIF] from uvm_test_top.env.agt.drv. Find the CFGDB/SET and CFGDB/GET lines for name='vif' and compare scope, name, type and order. Fix the driver so that it gets exactly the type tb_top publishes and still drives through the driver_mp modport view, then rerun.

steps.title: Step 2: Fix the monitor
steps.instructions: The run now stops with the same NO_VIF message from uvm_test_top.env.agt.mon. Compare its CFGDB/GET line with the CFGDB/SET line: the type and the scope match, so what differs? Fix the monitor and rerun.

steps.title: Step 3: Find the setting that nobody read
steps.instructions: The run completes but ends with UVM_ERROR [CHK] expected 6 transfers, monitor saw 4. Read the CFGNRD report that check_config_usage() prints in end_of_elaboration_phase: the test's own num_pkts setting was never read. Work out which component should read it and why its path does not match the scope, then fix the test's set().

steps.title: Step 4: Predict, then fix the precedence surprise
steps.instructions: Before you rerun, predict whether the agent will print num_pkts=4 or num_pkts=6, and say which precedence rule decides it. Rerun and explain the result. Then fix the bench so that the test's value wins without moving the test's set() out of build_phase.

steps.title: Step 5: Confirm a clean run
steps.instructions: The final run prints six [DRV] Driving pins through the clocking block lines, [AGT] num_pkts=6, no CFGNRD list, [CHK] PASS: monitor saw 6 transfers, and a report summary with UVM_ERROR : 0 and UVM_FATAL : 0. Compare your files with the solution files and answer the three questions in Step 5 of the README.
